proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, printed proof of Theorem 1.2 (p. 208): "if x ∈ M is one of the μ_V-almost all points such that η_V^(x) exists, and if β is a non-negative continuous function on G(n + ℓ, n), then we evidently have η_V^(x)(β) = θ(x)β(T_x)". ERRATUM (documented in the parent proof): this must read η_V^(x)(β) = β(T_x), because the averages of Lemma 1.3 are normalised by μ_V(B_ρ(x)), so the multiplicity cancels. This child proves the corrected claim in limit form; the argument is Step 2 (a)–(d) of the parent proof, made self-contained (the denominator limit is obtained as the case β ≡ 1 of the numerator limit, so no density lemma is needed).

Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (a compact space); μ := V.weight; B_r(y) := closedBall y r; Gₙ(A) := A ×ˢ univ; |·| is the Euclidean norm; ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal; H^n := μHE[n]; t^{-n} := (t⁻¹)^n. For β ∈ C(G) and t > 0 put J_β(t) := t^{-n} ∫_{B_t(x) × G} β(S) dV(y, S) (Bochner set integral over B_t(x) ×ˢ univ). The hypothesis HasTangentPlane V x T θ means: x ∈ U, 0 < θ, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G), ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) → θ ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) as t → 0⁺.

1. ω ∈ (0, ∞). unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : ℝ^n) 1) is positive (a nonempty open set has positive additive-Haar measure: Metric.measure_ball_pos) and finite (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence 0 < ω.

2. Local finiteness at x. U is open (V.isOpen_domain) and x ∈ U, so there is δ > 0 with ball x δ ⊆ U; put r₀ := δ/4. For 0 < t ≤ r₀, B_{2t}(x) ⊆ B_{δ/2}(x) ⊆ U and B_{2r₀}(x) is compact, so V(B_{2t}(x) × G) ≤ V(B_{2r₀}(x) × G) < ∞ (V.finite_on_compact). Hence, for 0 < t ≤ r₀, every bounded Borel function on ℝ^N × G vanishing outside B_{2t}(x) × G is V-integrable.

3. Cut-offs. For 0 < a < b let χ_{a,b}(y) := max(0, min(1, (b − |y|)/(b − a))). Then χ_{a,b} is continuous, 0 ≤ χ_{a,b} ≤ 1, χ_{a,b}(y) = 1 if |y| ≤ a, and χ_{a,b}(y) = 0 if |y| ≥ b; so χ_{a,b} vanishes outside the compact set B_b(0). For β ∈ C(G), f_{a,b,β}(y, S) := χ_{a,b}(y) β(S) is continuous on ℝ^N × G and vanishes outside B_b(0) × G, which is compact since G is compact; hence f_{a,b,β} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G).

4. Both sides of Def. 1.1 on f := f_{a,b,β}. (a) For t > 0, rescaledMeasure V x t = ENNReal.ofReal(t⁻¹ ^ n) • V.measure.map φ_t with φ_t(y, S) := (t⁻¹ • (y − x), S), which is continuous, hence measurable. By integral_smul_measure, (ENNReal.ofReal(t⁻¹ ^ n)).toReal = t⁻¹ ^ n (as t⁻¹ ^ n ≥ 0), and integral_map (f is continuous, hence AE-strongly measurable),
 ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = t^{-n} ∫ χ_{a,b}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) β(S) dV(y, S).
 (b) planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^n.restrict T.plane).map (y ↦ (y, T)); by integral_map and integral_mul_const,
 ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) = ∫_{T.plane} χ_{a,b}(y) β(T) dH^n(y) = β(T) c_{a,b}, where c_{a,b} := ∫_{T.plane} χ_{a,b} dH^n.
 Hence, by HasTangentPlane applied to f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G):
 (★) I_{a,b,β}(t) := t^{-n} ∫ χ_{a,b}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) β(S) dV(y, S) → θ β(T) c_{a,b} as t → 0⁺.

5. Plane balls. For s ≥ 0, H^n(T.plane ∩ B_s(0)) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n; in particular (H^n(T.plane ∩ B_s(0))).toReal = ω s^n. Proof: P := T.plane has finrank P = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane), so it has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n, b := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P).reindex (finCongr T.finrank_plane), and e := b.repr.symm : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ P is a linear isometry equivalence. The composite ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^N, ι(v) := (e v : ℝ^N), is an isometry (P.subtypeₗᵢ.isometry.comp e.isometry) with ι(0) = 0 and |ι(v)| = |v|; hence ι(B_s(0)) = P ∩ B_s(0) (⊆: e v ∈ P and |ι v| = |v| ≤ s; ⊇: for y ∈ P ∩ B_s(0), v := e.symm ⟨y, _⟩ has ι(v) = y and |v| = |y| ≤ s). Therefore
 H^n(P ∩ B_s(0)) = H^n(ι(B_s(0))) = μHE[n]_{ℝ^n}(B_s(0)) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) = volume(B_s(0)) (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume) = ENNReal.ofReal(s^n) * volume(ball(0, 1)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall with finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n (definition of unitBallVolume, ENNReal.ofReal_pow for s ≥ 0, commutativity).
 This argument is uniform in n, including n = 0 (where both sides equal 1).

6. Plane integrals. Let 0 < κ < 1. By 3, 1_{B_{1−κ}(0)} ≤ χ_{1−κ,1} and χ_{1,1+κ} ≤ 1_{B_{1+κ}(0)} pointwise. All these functions are bounded, Borel and vanish outside a compact set, and H^n.restrict T.plane is finite on compact sets (by 5), so they are integrable; monotonicity of the integral and 5 give
 c_{1−κ,1} ≥ (H^n(T.plane ∩ B_{1−κ}(0))).toReal = ω (1 − κ)^n and c_{1,1+κ} ≤ (H^n(T.plane ∩ B_{1+κ}(0))).toReal = ω (1 + κ)^n.

7. Squeeze for β ≥ 0. Let β ∈ C(G) with β ≥ 0 and 0 < κ < 1. For t > 0 and every y,
 χ_{1−κ,1}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(y) ≤ χ_{1,1+κ}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)):
 if |y − x| ≤ t then |t⁻¹ • (y − x)| ≤ 1, so χ_{1,1+κ}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) = 1 = 1_{B_t(x)}(y) ≥ χ_{1−κ,1}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)); if |y − x| > t then |t⁻¹ • (y − x)| > 1, so χ_{1−κ,1}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) = 0 = 1_{B_t(x)}(y) ≤ χ_{1,1+κ}(t⁻¹ • (y − x)).
 Multiply by β(S) ≥ 0 and integrate against V. For 0 < t ≤ r₀ all three integrands are bounded Borel functions vanishing outside B_{2t}(x) × G (because (1 + κ)t < 2t), hence V-integrable by 2, and the middle integral is ∫_{B_t(x)×G} β(S) dV (integral_indicator, B_t(x) ×ˢ univ being Borel). So by integral_mono, for 0 < t ≤ r₀,
 I_{1−κ,1,β}(t) ≤ J_β(t) ≤ I_{1,1+κ,β}(t).
 Put L := θ ω β(T) (≥ 0) and let ε > 0. Since θ β(T) ω (1 − κ)^n → L and θ β(T) ω (1 + κ)^n → L as κ → 0⁺, fix κ ∈ (0, 1) with θ β(T) ω (1 − κ)^n > L − ε/2 and θ β(T) ω (1 + κ)^n < L + ε/2. By (★), 6, θ > 0 and β(T) ≥ 0, eventually as t → 0⁺:
 I_{1−κ,1,β}(t) > θ β(T) c_{1−κ,1} − ε/2 ≥ θ β(T) ω (1 − κ)^n − ε/2 > L − ε, and
 I_{1,1+κ,β}(t) < θ β(T) c_{1,1+κ} + ε/2 ≤ θ β(T) ω (1 + κ)^n + ε/2 < L + ε.
 Together with the squeeze (valid for t ≤ r₀), L − ε < J_β(t) < L + ε eventually as t → 0⁺. As ε > 0 was arbitrary, J_β(t) → θ ω β(T) as t → 0⁺ (tendsto_order).

8. General β. For β ∈ C(G) let β⁺ := max(β, 0) and β⁻ := max(−β, 0); both belong to C(G), are ≥ 0, and β = β⁺ − β⁻. For 0 < t ≤ r₀ their integrals over B_t(x) × G are finite (2), so J_β(t) = J_{β⁺}(t) − J_{β⁻}(t) (integral_sub). By 7, J_β(t) → θ ω (β⁺(T) − β⁻(T)) = θ ω β(T) as t → 0⁺.

9. Denominator. For the constant function 1 ∈ C(G): ∫_{B_t(x)×G} 1 dV = (V(B_t(x) × G)).toReal = (μ(B_t(x))).toReal (setIntegral_const; Varifold.weight_apply, closed balls being Borel). So by 8, t^{-n} (μ(B_t(x))).toReal = J_1(t) → θ ω as t → 0⁺, and θ ω ≠ 0 by θ > 0 and 1.

10. Ratio. For t > 0, t^{-n} ≠ 0, hence (∫_{B_t(x)×G} β(S) dV) / (μ(B_t(x))).toReal = J_β(t) / J_1(t) (mul_div_mul_left; this also holds when the denominator vanishes, both sides then being 0). By 8, 9 and Tendsto.div with nonzero limit, J_β(t)/J_1(t) → θ ω β(T)/(θ ω) = β(T). Since the two functions agree on (0, ∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, the quotient in the statement tends to β(T) as ρ → 0⁺. ∎
